exposure: being known to child protection services
cohort: The study included 25,407 culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) Australian women in Sydney, New South Wales.
finding: Antenatal distress and depressive symptoms were associated with a lack of partner support, intimate partner violence, maternal history of childhood abuse, and being known to child protection services, while higher socioeconomic status had a protective effect against antenatal and postnatal depressive symptoms.
